official_sources: Appeals guide applications on or after 1 April 2026
Appeals guide applications on or before 31 March 2026
Town and Country Planning Act 1990 section 78

official_measurement_examples.name: 1 April 2026 split
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Inspectorate maintains separate procedural guides based on whether the underlying application was dated on or before 31 March 2026 or on/after 1 April 2026.

official_measurement_examples.name: Right to appeal
official_measurement_examples.fact: Section 78 appeals can arise from refusal, objectionable conditions or non-determination, subject to the applicable statutory route and time limit.

official_measurement_examples.name: Procedure determination
official_measurement_examples.fact: Written representations, hearing and inquiry are distinct procedures; the Planning Inspectorate determines the appropriate procedure.

official_measurement_examples.name: Part 1 evidence control
official_measurement_examples.fact: For many post-1 April 2026 appeals under Part 1 written representations, the Inspector normally considers the application material previously before the LPA rather than allowing a new case to be built.

official_measurement_examples.name: Appeal is not permission
official_measurement_examples.fact: Lodging or validating an appeal does not itself grant planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Interested-party comments
official_measurement_examples.fact: For many new-system Part 1 appeals there is no new appeal-stage comment opportunity; application-stage representations are carried forward.

official_measurement_examples.name: Costs are separate
official_measurement_examples.fact: An award of appeal costs concerns unreasonable behaviour and expense; it is separate from whether the appeal succeeds on planning merits.

official_measurement_examples.name: Parcel limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Appeal status does not establish ownership, implementation, other consents or final development yield.

core_rules: appeal submission is not planning permission
appeal validation is not appeal success
pre and post 1 April 2026 procedure guides remain distinct
appeal time limit depends on appeal type
Part1 evidence restrictions must be retained
written representations hearing and inquiry are distinct
costs award is separate from planning merits
appeal decision does not establish ownership
appeal does not replace other statutory consents
dismissal is not universal site prohibition
allowance can remain subject to conditions
linked enforcement/LDC appeal rules are case-specific
called-in application is distinct from appeal
no parcel appeal clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Planning Inspectorate and GOV.UK appeal guidance checked 2026-07-26, including both procedural guides updated 16 July 2026 and the post-1 April 2026 Part 1 system.
